title: NoSQL Database Families
content: NoSQL databases fall into four families. Document databases such as MongoDB store JSON-like BSON documents with a flexible schema and can index fields inside the document. Key-value stores such as Redis map one key to one opaque value and give constant-time lookups, which suits caching and session storage. Wide-column stores such as Apache Cassandra organise rows by partition key and are built for very high write throughput, time-series and IoT data. Graph databases such as Neo4j store nodes and relationships and are optimised for multi-hop traversal like friend-of-a-friend or fraud rings.

title: BSON and Schema Design
content: MongoDB stores data as BSON, a binary form of JSON that adds real types such as ObjectId, Date, Decimal128 and binary data. Schema design is driven by access patterns. Embedding puts related data inside one document so it is read in a single operation; it suits one-to-few, bounded relationships such as a course and its schedule. Referencing stores related data in a separate collection linked by an id; it suits unbounded or many-to-many relationships such as comments on a popular post. A single document is limited to 16 MB, so unbounded embedded arrays are an anti-pattern. JSON Schema validators can enforce required fields and types on a collection.

title: CRUD and the Query Language
content: PyMongo exposes insert_one, insert_many, find, find_one, update_one, update_many, replace_one, delete_one and delete_many. Query filters use comparison operators like $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in and $ne, logical operators like $or, $and and $not, and $elemMatch for matching several conditions on one array element. Projections choose which fields are returned, and skip with limit implements pagination. An upsert updates a matching document or inserts a new one atomically. $set is idempotent when retried, while $inc and $mul are not idempotent, which matters when writes are retried after a timeout.

title: Aggregation Framework
content: The aggregation framework processes documents through a pipeline of stages. $match filters documents and should come first so later stages handle less data. $group computes accumulators such as $sum, $avg, $min, $max and $push for each group key, similar to SQL GROUP BY. $sort orders results and $limit keeps the top N. $project reshapes documents, $unwind flattens an array into one document per element, and $lookup performs a left outer join with another collection. $facet runs several sub-pipelines in parallel and $bucket groups values into ranges.

title: Indexing and Query Performance
content: Without an index MongoDB performs a COLLSCAN and examines every document. With a suitable index explain() shows an IXSCAN and totalDocsExamined drops sharply. Compound indexes serve queries on a left-to-right prefix of their fields. The ESR rule orders compound index fields as Equality first, then Sort, then Range. Every extra index slows inserts and updates because the index must be maintained on each write. A covered query is answered from the index alone when the filter and projection use only indexed fields and exclude _id, so no documents are fetched.

title: Replica Sets and High Availability
content: A replica set is a group of mongod processes holding the same data. One primary accepts all writes and records them in the oplog; secondaries replicate the oplog and can serve reads when the read preference allows it. If the primary becomes unreachable the remaining members hold an election and a secondary with a majority of votes becomes the new primary, usually within about ten to twelve seconds. Member priority biases which node wins. An arbiter votes in elections but stores no data. Drivers detect the new primary automatically and retryable writes hide short failovers from the application.

title: CAP Theorem, Write Concern and Transactions
content: The CAP theorem says a distributed system facing a network partition must choose between consistency and availability. MongoDB favours consistency: only the side of a partition holding a majority can elect a primary and accept writes. Write concern controls acknowledgement: w:1 waits for the primary only, w:majority waits for a majority of voting members, and j:true waits for the journal to be written to disk, so stronger settings add latency. Multi-document ACID transactions use a session, read concern snapshot and write concern majority; they need a replica set and abort entirely on error, as in a bank transfer that must debit and credit together.

title: Sharding and Horizontal Scaling
content: Sharding partitions a collection across several shards so data and load scale horizontally. A mongos router sends each query to the shards that own the relevant chunks, and config servers store the cluster metadata. A good shard key has high cardinality, an even frequency distribution, appears in most query filters for targeted routing, and is not monotonically increasing. A timestamp or auto-increment shard key creates a hotspot because every new insert lands on the last chunk. Hashed shard keys spread inserts evenly but turn range queries into scatter-gather queries.

title: Security and Operations
content: Database security follows the CIA triad of confidentiality, integrity and availability. Authentication with SCRAM verifies users, and role-based access control grants built-in roles such as read and readWrite or custom roles scoped to specific collections, following least privilege. TLS encrypts data in transit, and encryption at rest protects files on disk. Views with $project can redact sensitive fields such as masking an SSN. In production, serverStatus exposes connections, opcounters and WiredTiger cache metrics for monitoring, and backups taken with mongodump must be verified by restoring them with mongorestore and comparing counts and checksums.

title: Vector Search and Retrieval Augmented Generation
content: An embedding model turns text into a dense vector so that texts with similar meaning are close under cosine similarity. MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores embeddings in a document field and builds an approximate nearest neighbour index based on HNSW, a layered navigable small-world graph that trades a little recall for much faster search than exact brute force. IVF is another ANN method that clusters vectors and searches only the nearest clusters. The $vectorSearch aggregation stage returns the top-k most similar chunks. Retrieval augmented generation retrieves relevant chunks and places them in the prompt so a language model answers from grounded context and can cite its sources, reducing hallucination.

title: Small and Large Language Models
content: Large language models such as GPT-4 class models have tens or hundreds of billions of parameters and are usually served from the cloud through an API. Small language models such as Llama 3.2 1B, Qwen2.5 1.5B, Phi-3 Mini and Gemma 2 2B have roughly one to four billion parameters and can run locally on a laptop CPU through Ollama, often with 4-bit quantisation. Both are decoder-only transformers that generate text one token at a time using self-attention. SLMs are cheaper, private and fast but have less world knowledge, which is why grounding them with retrieved context from a database matters even more.

title: Containers and Deployment
content: Docker packages each service with its dependencies into an image, and Docker Compose starts several containers on a shared network where they reach each other by service name rather than localhost. Inside a container, localhost refers to that container itself, so a frontend must call the backend at http://backend:8000. Named volumes keep MongoDB data when containers are recreated. Kubernetes runs MongoDB as a StatefulSet with a headless service so each pod keeps a stable network identity and its own persistent volume. Terraform can provision MongoDB Atlas clusters as infrastructure as code.
